text: City Attorney Impartial Analysis — Measure D

Measure D would amend Chapter 4.09.025, "Tax Rate," of Chapter 4.09 of Title 4 of the Burlingame Municipal Code, to increase Burlingame's Transient Occupancy Tax rate by three percentage points, from 12% to 15%.

Transient Occupancy Tax ("TOT" or "hotel tax") is paid on temporary lodging at hotels, motels, inns, and other short-term lodgings of less than 30 continuous days. The hotel guest is responsible for paying the tax.

The Cityof Burlingame received approximately $22 million in TOT revenue in Fiscal Year 2025-2026. If D would generate an estimated additional $5.7 million annually, based on existing occupancy rates, room rates, and total number of hotel rooms in Burlingame.

Measure-D is a general tax. If the measure is adopted, the proceeds would go into the General Fund. Those revenues may be used for unrestricted governmental purposes such as repairing and maintaining City streets, sidewalks and infrastructure; maintaining City parks and trees; enhancing public safety and emergency preparedness; and general government uses. These revenues cannot be taken away by the State.

Measure D proceeds would be subject to the same annual audit requirements as other General Fund revenues. Any auditor's report shall include an accounting of the revenues received from the Transient Occupancy Tax and shall be presented to the City Council annually and made available for public review.
The Burlingame City Council placed Measure D on the November 2026 ballot.

As a general tax, Measure D requires a simple majority for approval, which is 50% + 1 of votes cast in favor. The tax would remain in place until amended or repealed by the voters. A "Yes" vote would approve amending the Transient Occupancy Tax rate from 12% to 15%. A "No" vote would reject the measure and keep the current 12% tax rate.
Michael Guina City Attorney

text: Argument in Favor of Measure Vote Yes on Measure to support a safe, strong Burlingame and protect local property values, all without raising taxes on residents. We live in Burlingame because it offers an exceptional quality of life and great local services. We take pride in our Police Department, parks, local businesses, and community programs for youth and seniors. However, the growing number of visitors who stay in our community has added pressure onto our streets, sidewalks, and public safety services. These community spaces, streets, and sidewalks now require ongoing maintenance that is beyond current available resources. If we don't address these issues now, they will be more expensive to repair and maintain in the future. Burlingame's hotel tax rate is currently among the lowest in the County and has not been increased in more than 17 years. Voting YES on Measure ensures that hotel guests help fund the services they use, so local homeowners and residents don't bear the full cost. Well-maintained streets, safe sidewalks, and clean parks protect Burlingame's quality of life and help preserve property values. Measure Does Not Increase Taxes for Local Residents Measure ensures our hotel guests pay their fair share for city services The state and federal government cannot take one penny of Measure Independent citizens' oversight and annual financial audits are required Vote YES on : Keep Burlingame Safe and Desirable Repair and maintain streets, sidewalks, and potholes Maintain parks and healthy trees on city streets 8 Strengthen emergency preparedness and public safety Support recreation programs and facilities for youth and seniors 9

Safe neighborhoods, beautiful parks and clean streets make Burlingame a desirable place to live, do business, and raise a family. Join local leaders in voting Yes on Measure to protect our community and keep Burlingame Strong.
